issue.title: just install silently accepts a dangling editable plugin install when the linked repo checkout is absent, so sase validate (and every just check) goes red
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-p4 land agent (2026-08-18) during that epic's landing verification, in workspace sase_13 (host project gh_sase-org__sase). Unrelated to sase-p4's diff.

SYMPTOM: 'just check' and 'just check-full' fail at the 'SASE validation' gate, which sits before the test lane, so the run aborts and every agent in the workspace gets a red check unrelated to its own diff:

  fail   doctor config.file_hooks
  Skipping invalid file hook 'sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights' from config layer 'user': unknown file-hook provider 'research-highlights'; install a plugin exposing the sase_file_hooks entry point group or remove 'use'
  error: recipe `validate` failed on line 786 with exit code 1
  error: recipe `check` failed on line 648 with exit code 1

The message is misleading: the entry point IS present in the venv metadata.

  importlib.metadata.entry_points(group='sase_file_hooks')
    → research-highlights -> sase_research_artifacts.provider:RESEARCH_HIGHLIGHTS_HOOK

ROOT CAUSE: the distribution's metadata is installed but its module is not importable, so the artifact-provider registry drops the provider and config.file_hooks then cannot resolve it. get_artifact_provider_registry() reports it directly:

  file hook providers: []
  ArtifactProviderDiagnostic(code='entry_point_load_failed',
    message="Failed to load artifact provider entry point sase_file_hooks:research-highlights: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase_research_artifacts'",
    severity='error', package='sase-research-artifacts', version='0.1.0')

sase-research-artifacts is installed EDITABLE, and its .pth points at a directory that does not exist in this workspace:

  .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_editable_impl_sase_research_artifacts.pth
    → <workspace>/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts/src   (No such file or directory)
  direct_url.json: {"url":"file://<workspace>/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts","dir_info":{"editable":true}}

Only sase/repos/linked/sase-core was materialized in this workspace; the sase-research-artifacts checkout was not.

WHY just install DOES NOT REPAIR IT: Justfile:184 _setup-required-plugins calls install_one, which prefers the linked source tree only when \${dir}/pyproject.toml exists and otherwise falls back to PyPI:

  install_one sase-research-artifacts \"{{ sase_research_artifacts_dir }}\"
  → [setup] Installing required plugin sase-research-artifacts from PyPI.
    Resolved 1 package in 130ms / Checked 1 package in 0.09ms

That reads as success, but sase-research-artifacts is NOT published to PyPI — 'uv pip install --reinstall sase-research-artifacts' fails with 'was not found in the package registry'. The plain install only 'succeeds' because uv sees the requirement already satisfied by the stale editable dist-info and short-circuits without resolving or validating that the target still exists. So the broken state is self-perpetuating across every just install.

REPRODUCTION: in a workspace whose sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts checkout is absent but whose venv still holds the editable install from a previous use: run 'just install' (reports success), then '.venv/bin/sase doctor -C config.file_hooks' → ERROR, or 'just check' → fails at SASE validation. '.venv/bin/python -c \"import sase_research_artifacts\"' → ModuleNotFoundError.

RECOVERY (what unblocked this landing): 'sase repo open sase-research-artifacts -r \"...\"' materializes the linked checkout, the .pth resolves again, the import works, doctor returns OK, and 'just check' reaches the test lane with every lint gate green.

SCOPE: make the required-plugin setup path fail loudly or self-heal instead of silently accepting a dangling editable install. Options, roughly in preference order: (1) after installing, verify each required plugin actually imports and its entry points load, and fail the setup with the recovery command when it does not; (2) when the linked source dir is missing but an editable install already points into it, materialize the linked checkout (the same thing sase repo open does) rather than falling back to PyPI; (3) do not fall back to PyPI for plugins that have no PyPI release — that branch can only ever no-op or fail confusingly.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-o6 — the same class of stale-install trap on the other side (the global 'sase' on PATH is a uv tool install pinned to a separate checkout). A live symptom of that one is visible in this very workspace: every global 'sase bead ...' invocation prints "unknown file-hook provider 'sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights'" — note the FULL prefixed id, not the bare name the workspace venv reports — because the global tool predates commit 54da09ba5 'feat(config)!: require plugin prefix on every use: field' and cannot parse the new prefixed 'use:' form the user's config now carries. Different root cause from this bead (a stale global tool vs. a dangling editable install), but a fix for either should consider whether the setup path can detect the other.

RELATED: sase-jw — 'sase_17 workspace's linked sase-core checkout is 8 commits stale, breaking just check/just install'. Same family (a workspace's linked-repo checkout out of step with what the venv expects) but a different root cause: sase-jw is a STALE checkout, this bead is an ABSENT one that leaves the editable install dangling and that just install then reports as satisfied.

RESOLVED BY EPIC sase-p3.15 — verification from sase-p3.15.land (2026-08-18, workspace sase_12, HEAD 11f78656d). This bead's exact root cause (uv treats a name-satisfied dist-info as installed, so _setup-required-plugins cannot replace a dangling editable install whose .pth points at an absent linked checkout) was the target of phase sase-p3.15.1, which replaced the Justfile recipe with tools/setup_required_plugins. That tool now spawns the target interpreter to 'import <module>' after every install attempt -- a fresh subprocess, because a newly written .pth is only processed by site at interpreter start -- and on failure forces one 'uv pip install --reinstall-package <name>' and re-checks. Observed firing for real in this workspace, not simulated: 'just install' printed '[setup] sase-github installed from PyPI but import sase_github failed; forcing a reinstall' and repaired it; the immediately following run of the same tool is a clean no-op at exit 0, so the repair is idempotent rather than a reinstall-every-time loop. Post-state: sase-github 0.2.5 and sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0 both importable, 'sase doctor -C plugins.required' OK with 2 required plugin(s) satisfied, and 'sase validate' exit 0 with 'ok doctor config.file_hooks' and no 'Skipping invalid file hook' line on stderr -- the precise symptom this bead reports. The misleading-message complaint is also addressed: when no source works the tool now exits with a message naming the plugin and the exact next command ('sase repo open <name>' for a linked plugin, otherwise the install command) instead of uv's raw resolution error. Two things this bead's description says are no longer true of the code: install_one and the sase_research_artifacts_dir Justfile variable are gone, and phase sase-p3.15.3 additionally pinned sase-research-artifacts>=0.2.0 now that 0.2.0 is on PyPI, so a fresh workspace with no linked checkout resolves from the index rather than needing 'sase repo open' at all. Flagging for triage as fixed rather than closing it myself, since a task bead's close is the owner's call.

Verified on clean master b7bdd3185 after just install. tools/setup_required_plugins, introduced by eed1d9a67, completed successfully; sase_github and sase_research_artifacts both import in the workspace interpreter; and sase doctor -C plugins.required reports OK with 2 required plugins satisfied. The tool now verifies imports in a fresh subprocess and performs a forced reinstall when metadata points at a broken editable checkout, which directly addresses the dangling-install mechanism in this bead.

payload.close_reason: Required-plugin setup now detects and repairs dangling editable installs; both required plugins import and the doctor check is green.
